articles.title: Covid-19: 'Lessons need to be learnt' as care home report published
articles.summary: An inquiry found that Government failings in care settings allowed the spread of Covid.
articles.body:
Lessons need to be learnt after an inquiry found that government failings in care settings allowed the spread of Covid, a woman whose mother died during the pandemic has said.

The sixth report from the Covid inquiry, which was published on Tuesday, said the care sector appeared to be "something of an afterthought" in the early stages of the pandemic and there was no "protective ring" put around homes as claimed by ministers at the time.

There were more than 43,000 recorded deaths involving Covid in care homes between March 2020 and July 2022.

Martina Ferguson, whose mother Ursula Derry died during the coronavirus pandemic, said "we need to learn from what's happened".

She said the report has "reopened, wounds for many families here in Northern Ireland".

"Many families in our bereaved group were prevented from being with loved ones when they were at their most vulnerable, you know, they stood outside windows trying to communicate through a glass.

"I did that for nine months when my mummy was in her care home."

About 1.5 million adults were either living in care homes or receiving support in their own homes when Covid hit.

Action to protect them came too late, causing devastating consequences, the inquiry said.

Speaking on BBC Radio Ulster's Good Morning Ulster programme , Ferguson said: "Years later, families are still carrying deep feelings of guilt and, despite having done absolutely nothing wrong, but they wonder whether their loved one felt, abandoned, frightened, or alone."

Ferguson has created Ursula's Law, a proposed legislative campaign in Northern Ireland that is named in her mum's memory, which aims to establish a statutory right for patients to designate a care partner across all health and social care settings.

Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

In 2016, Prof Raphael Bengoa published a review that was supposed to change the way Northern Ireland does healthcare.

Ferguson makes reference to the report and said that "when you look at what happened, bereaved families and other families during the pandemic, guidance completely failed us during the pandemic".

"If we face another health crisis or a pandemic, we face, in my opinion, utter chaos in healthcare settings because the trust is totally broken and people simply won't comply," she added.

She said if Stormont is serious about Bengoa's report and improving the health care system they "must enshrine this absolute right in law" for patients to designate an essential family carer.

The 287-page report also highlighted shortages of personal protective equipment for carers and criticised the way hospital patients were discharged into care homes.

It said limits on visits caused enormous harm to residents and their loved ones, though it blamed this on care homes themselves.

Pauline Shepherd, chief executive of Independent Health & Care Providers, said the "government's response to Covid in care homes was much too little, too late".

"It was a horrific time for people living in the care homes, their families and the staff that were caring for them."

articles.title: Former McDonald's exec spills the beans on why healthier menu favorite got the axe
articles.summary: McDonald's grilled chicken sandwich disappeared in 2020 after sales dipped too low, but rising beef prices could bring chicken options back.
articles.body: McDonald's is looking to expand its chicken offerings, including potentially bringing back grilled chicken sandwiches — a menu item the fast-food giant discontinued in 2020. At a September investor meeting, McDonald's executives discussed plans to expand the chain's chicken lineup, including grilled chicken sandwiches and wraps, as demand for protein options grows, according to Restaurant Dive. The renewed interest comes years after McDonald's pulled its grilled chicken sandwich from U.S. menus, raising questions about why the healthier offering disappeared in the first place. MCDONALD'S EXECUTIVE REVEALS SIMPLE MENU HACKS TO HELP CUSTOMERS PACK MORE PROTEIN INTO MEALS Chef Mike Haracz, who served as McDonald's manager of culinary innovation from 2015 to 2019, told Fox News Digital why the grilled chicken sandwich ultimately failed to make the cut — and whether it could find its way back to the menu. The reason was simple: Not enough customers were ordering it, Haracz said. "For many of the menu items at McDonald's, and this is true for any corporate chain restaurant, there is a certain sales threshold that means it will be profitable, and it makes sense to have in the restaurant," said Haracz, who is based in Illinois. "Once sales dip below a certain level, it does not make financial sense to keep it on the menu, as you will end up throwing away product." In 1993, McDonald's introduced a grilled chicken sandwich as a healthier menu offering, but it did not stand the test of time. MCDONALD'S BRINGS BACK POPULAR ITEM FOR SHORT TIME AS ONE STATE GETS A TREAT The sandwich consisted of a marinated skinless chicken breast filet, lettuce, tomato, sweet red onion, Monterey Jack cheese and a herb sauce, all piled on a bun, according to a 1993 press release about the menu item. McDonald's unveiled a more natural preparation of its grilled chicken in 2015, announcing on its website that it would be cooked using only canola oil, olive oil, and real spices and herbs. The chain revamped the sandwich that year, introducing the Artisan Grilled Chicken Sandwich. Ultimately, though, the grilled chicken sandwich lost its spot at McDonald's in 2020, when the chain also removed salads from its U.S. menus, according to Business Insider. In his role at McDonald's, Haracz formulated new menu items for U.S. locations. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER People looking for healthier options at McDonald's appreciated the grilled chicken offering — especially parents, Haracz noted, because while their kids might have been excited about eating a Happy Meal, the parents were not as interested. Like many other menu items, the grilled chicken sandwich was cooked on a flattop and held in the universal holding cabinets (UHCs). Ultimately, it came down to simple dollars and cents. Space is valuable at McDonald's, Haracz noted, with each location organized to make every square inch profitable. Consumer satisfaction played a big role, Haracz said, adding that he thinks the grilled chicken sandwich's flavor profile didn't always wow guests. "McDonald's also realized once it gets to a point, there may be menu cannibalization, [which] means instead of ordering Chicken McNuggets, I might order the chicken sandwich," Haracz said. "Well, if we take the chicken sandwich away, are they still going to order Chicken McNuggets or other items? Most likely they are." "I do think there's a chance it could come back because many chains are dealing with the fact that beef prices are rising, and a way to offset that is to offer a more affordable protein option, which would be chicken," he said. Haracz said he's not sure if there will be a renaissance of grilled chicken specifically. articles.summary: For most people, a summer escape means booking a flight, packing a suitcase and leaving home behind.
articles.body: For most people, a summer escape means booking a flight, packing a suitcase and leaving home behind. For Michael Scherrer, the holiday destination is considerably closer. In his garden in Switzerland, the 48-year-old content creator has spent a year transforming a modest patch of land into a miniature Greek village, complete with cobbled lanes, blue shutters and a traditional-style bar. Built with the help of his brother Samuel, 46, the project turns the idea of a backyard makeover into something closer to a private theme park. Scroll down to read the details.A Greek escape at homeAccording to a Daily Mail report, the Greek village occupies a 15-by-15-metre section of the garden and cost around £10,000 to create. Its design is intended to evoke the character of a Mediterranean holiday, with winding stone pathways, tiny buildings, vivid blue details and carefully designed spaces that encourage visitors to linger.At the centre of the experience is a small bar, positioned so that guests can sit surrounded by the village rather than simply looking at it from the outside. The effect is deliberately immersive, creating the sensation of stepping into another country without leaving the property, adds the online report.On the other hand, PEOPLE reported that Scherrer built the village as a place where he and his clients could sit and talk, but the project quickly became much more ambitious. Planning permissions and unpredictable weather in Switzerland extended the construction process, turning what began as a gardening and building project into a substantial long-term undertaking.From garden to theme parkThe Greek village is only one part of a much larger attraction. Scherrer and his brother have around 1,500 square metres available for their creative projects and have so far developed approximately 600 square metres.The wider garden has already taken on the character of a miniature theme park, with spaces inspired by different countries, ideas and seasons. Alongside the Greek setting is a Japanese garden, while an Irish bar and Halloween-themed areas add contrasting moods to the landscape, adds the Daily Mail report.The project has cost approximately £20,000 overall, with each section designed to offer a different visual experience. Rather than following one consistent aesthetic, the brothers have embraced the garden as a constantly evolving collection of themed environments, adds the report.A backdrop for unexpected holidaysThe miniature village has also become an unlikely social-media prop. Its convincing details have allowed friends and family to take photographs that appear, at first glance, to have been taken abroad.The Daily Mail reported on the unusual backyard transformation, highlighting how visitors have used the setting to fool friends and colleagues into believing they have actually travelled to Greece. The illusion works precisely because of the attention paid to details such as the architecture, colour palette and layout of the tiny village.For Scherrer, however, the appeal goes beyond photographs. The garden provides a physical escape during the summer, creating a space where ordinary evenings can take on the atmosphere of a Mediterranean getaway.The next chapterAs per PEOPLE, the village is not necessarily finished. Scherrer has considered turning one of the tiny homes into a guest room, potentially adding a bed during spring so visitors could stay within the miniature setting.There are also plans for new themed areas, including a fishing village and another room for guests. The garden is still evolving, with a pirate ship among the possibilities.Small world gardens that tell stories and grow plants are popular. What began with two brothers wanting to garden and build has evolved into an imaginative landscape where Greece, Japan, Ireland and seasonal fantasy can coexist within a single Swiss backyard.Images Courtesy: Instagram/smallest_themeparkYou use AI every day. articles.title: Delhi AQI jumps from 179 to 244 in a day; GRAP-1 restrictions kick in across NCR
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated to the ‘poor’ category on Wednesday, prompting the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to invoke
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated to the ‘poor’ category on Wednesday, prompting the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to invoke Stage 1 measures under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across the National Capital Region (NCR) with immediate effect.Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI), which stood at 179 in the ‘moderate’ category on October 20, rose to 244 by 2pm on October 21, according to the CAQM order, news agency PTI reported.The sub-committee on GRAP took the decision after reviewing the prevailing air quality, meteorological forecasts and pollution levels.Forecasts by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) indicated that Delhi’s AQI was likely to remain in the ‘poor’ category over the coming days.What restrictions come under GRAP-1?Under Stage 1 of GRAP, the use of coal and firewood as fuel in tandoors at hotels, restaurants and open eateries is prohibited.The use of diesel generator sets is restricted, with exemptions for emergency and essential services as specified under the plan, PTI reported.The CAQM has directed agencies concerned across the NCR to implement the measures immediately and ensure that air quality does not deteriorate further.It has also urged citizens to follow the restrictions and cooperate with enforcement agencies.GRAP is a set of emergency measures implemented in stages to prevent further deterioration in air quality. The restrictions become progressively stricter as pollution levels rise.How are the GRAP stages triggered?Stage 1 is invoked when the AQI is in the ‘poor’ category, between 201 and 300.Stage 2 applies to the ‘very poor’ category, with AQI between 301 and 400.Stage 3 is triggered when the AQI is between 401 and 450, while Stage 4 applies when it exceeds 450.What other anti-pollution measures has Delhi announced?The GRAP-1 action comes days after the Delhi government announced its winter action plan to tackle air pollution.The plan, scheduled to run from November 1 to February 28, includes a ban on the entry of vehicles registered outside Delhi that do not meet BS-VI emission standards.The government has also announced a ‘No PUC, No Fuel’ policy, under which vehicles without a valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate will not be allowed to buy fuel at petrol pumps.Other measures include restrictions on construction and demolition activities, checks on the transportation of construction materials and steps to control road dust.The government has also proposed measures to promote public transport and electric buses as part of its broader effort to curb pollution during the winter months.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Masked boy guilty of trying to murder schoolgirl in Norfolk
articles.summary: The school went into lockdown and parents gathered at the gates as they waited for news about their children.
articles.body:
A teenage boy who had a hatred of women and an "obsessive interest" in killers has been found guilty of the attempted murder of a girl at his school.

The boy dressed in black and wore a face mask before stabbing the 15-year-old victim in the back at Thorpe St Andrew School, near Norwich, in March.

Armed police were called to the school, which went into lockdown, and the attack was caught on CCTV.

The boy, who is 16 and cannot be named for legal reasons, wrote notes about hating women and had an "obsessive and dangerous interest in killers and killing", jurors at King's Lynn Crown Court were told. He will be sentenced on 18 December.

Jurors deliberated for just under four hours before delivering a majority verdict at the end of a trial which began two weeks ago.

The teenager "went to school not to learn, but to kill" while armed with a kitchen knife, the prosecution said.

The school went into lockdown after the attack and there was an armed police response, while the girl was taken to hospital with a minor injury.

CCTV footage captured the moment the girl was stabbed in the back, before her attacker ran off while "pursued by a teacher".

The victim described to the jury how, in the aftermath of the attack, she had told a teacher "Sir, I've been stabbed" .

In a police interview played to the court, the girl said she was in "panic mode" and felt numb and weak.

Chris Paxton KC, prosecuting, said it was "sheer good fortune" the "defenceless and vulnerable" pupil was not seriously hurt.

"This was a knife strike delivered, we the prosecution say, as an attempt to kill," he added.

He messaged his mother to say "I'm sorry" shortly after the attack, jurors heard.

"I was in complete shock," she told the court.

Paxton said that in a note written before the attack, the would-be killer had written: "I really want to do it, really bad, I hate having to wait."

The note continued: "Motive = misanthropy, misogyny, suicide, bullying. Weapon = knife x2? Death = 2+ hopefully, injuries a lot hopefully."

Jurors heard he had a hatred of women and an "obsessive and dangerous interest in killers and killing".

The boy, who was 15 at the time, had pleaded guilty to possessing a kitchen knife without lawful authority and wounding with intent, but prosecutors proceeded with the attempted murder charge.

The boy did not give evidence during his trial. Instead, his barrister argued he could not have intended to kill the girl because he used "limited force" with the blade.

Having been found guilty, the judge Mr Justice Lickley warned the boy: "I'm sure you understand because of the very serious nature of the offence I will have to consider not only a custodial sentence, but one of some considerable length."

He nodded and replied "yes sir" before being led to the cells.

articles.title: Author Helen Fielding launches award to find the next Bridget Jones's Diary
articles.summary: The Bridget Jones Prize will go to the author of the funniest 1,000-word diary-style piece of writing.
articles.body:
Bridget Jones author Helen Fielding has launched a new prize aimed at discovering funny diary writers from the north of England, saying opportunities across the UK are "very uneven".

West Yorkshire-born Fielding, who penned Bridget's famous diary as well co-writing the film adaptations, has set up the Bridget Jones Prize with charity New Writing North.

The award will go to the person who submits the funniest 1,000-word piece of first-person writing.

Speaking at an event for the Independent, which first published Bridget's diary in 1995, Fielding said the spread of opportunity for writing in the UK is "very uneven", adding: "There's much more opportunity in the south than in the north, where I grew up."

The winner of the new prize - set to run for an initial three years from 2027 to 2029 - will receive a £2,000 prize and a package of writing support from Fielding's literary agents and New Writing North.

Fielding's original newspaper column went on to be published as a best-selling novel titled Bridget Jones's Diary in 1996.

It spawned several sequels and hit movie adaptations starring Renée Zellweger as the endearingly chaotic and lovelorn thirty-something diarist.

In a statement announcing the prize , Fielding noted how the "comedy heart" of Bridget's story came from the "everyday humour of people around me when growing up in Yorkshire: laughing together at our mess-ups; bringing the fancy and pretentious down to earth".

"There are lots of famous northern comics," said the writer, whose own work was inspired by the likes of Victoria Wood, Alan Bennett and Morecambe and Wise.

"But this prize is for the comic voices of people who aren't famous: just living their lives being quietly hilarious."

The Bridget Jones Prize will be awarded to an unpublished writer, without an agent, based in the north of England as part of New Writing North's Northern Writers' Awards.

Submissions will be open from 23 November 2026 to 1 February 2027.

The winner will be announced at the Northern Writers' Awards ceremony in Newcastle next summer, and will be presented with the award by Fielding.

Will Mackie from New Writing North said: "This is the first time the Northern Writers' Awards have featured an award exclusively for comedy writing.

"There is no-one more fitting to identify an original comedy voice than Helen, who created one of the nation's most beloved comic characters of the last 30 years."

articles.title: Badr accord: Turkey, Pak, Qatar & Indonesia ink defence pact; what it means for India
articles.summary: Türkiye, Qatar, Indonesia and Pakistan have signed the Badr memorandum to strengthen defence cooperation and develop strategic partnerships, the Turkish
articles.body: Türkiye, Qatar, Indonesia and Pakistan have signed the Badr memorandum to strengthen defence cooperation and develop strategic partnerships, the Turkish National Defence Ministry said on Wednesday.The agreement was signed in Doha by the defence ministers of the four countries, including Turkish National Defence Minister Yasar Guler, Qatar’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of State for Defence Affairs Sheikh Saud bin Abdulrahman bin Hasan Al Thani, Indonesian Deputy Defence Minister Yusuf Jauhari and Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif. Haluk Gorgun, head of Türkiye’s Presidency of Defence Industries, also attended the signing ceremony.What does the Badr memorandum cover?Named “Badr”, meaning “full moon”, the agreement aims to expand cooperation in military production, strengthen defence capabilities and promote collaboration in technical military training, research and development, the ministry said.The initiative is also intended to support the development of solutions and industrial sectors in line with advances in modern defence systems.According to the ministry, the agreement carries economic significance for the participating countries by combining their military production capabilities, improving integration and strengthening their defence industries to meet the requirements of allied and friendly countries.The memorandum is also expected to deepen defence industry ties, expand military cooperation and strengthen multilateral collaboration in support of security, stability and shared objectives.Should India be worried?The agreement brings Turkey, Pakistan, Qatar and Indonesia together under a framework for closer military and defence industry cooperation.Its stated objectives include joint production, capability development, training and research.Pakistan, which has long sought to offset India’s conventional military advantage through external partnerships, could gain greater strategic depth. Closer defence cooperation with Turkey, in particular, could strengthen Pakistan’s access to military technology, including drones, naval platforms and other defence systems.If the accord facilitates deeper integration between the participating countries' defence industries, it could help Pakistan diversify its arms procurement and sustain its military modernisation.For India, the concern would be the possibility of a more capable and better-connected Pakistani military, rather than the creation of an immediate, unified military threat. The drone and naval dimensions deserve particular attention as Turkey has developed significant capabilities in unmanned aerial systems, electronic warfare and naval platforms.India will also need to assess the Badr Accord alongside the separate Mecca Joint Defence Agreement between Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, signed in August 2026.Unlike the Badr memorandum, the Mecca pact provides for mutual defence assistance in the event of an armed attack. The two arrangements could complement each other if defence-industrial cooperation is accompanied by deeper intelligence-sharing, military coordination and logistical support. But they remain distinct agreements, and the Badr Accord itself does not establish a Nato-style collective-defence commitment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Kansas soccer field crash raises red flags for former investigator who questions key theories
articles.summary: Jamie Copenhaver, a former detective, questions why no charges were filed after a driver killed two at Wichita's Stryker Sports Complex.
articles.body: "Law enforcement certainly needed to do a better job as to describing why these charges haven't been filed," says Jamie Copenhaver. Copenhaver, a former sheriff's detective in Florida who worked with an FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force, is curious as to why law enforcement has been tight-lipped about the lack of charges in the horrific Kansas soccer field crash. A mother walked away with no charges after investigators say she drove onto the active field at Stryker Sports Complex where children and families were present — killing two and injuring several others. CHILD AMONG 2 KILLED AFTER VEHICLE DRIVES ONTO SOCCER FIELD AT KANSAS SPORTS COMPLEX It happened on Saturday; Cole Adrian, 6, and Nicholas Schafer, 35, who were both from McPherson, were killed. The woman behind the wheel was released after being interviewed by investigators that day. Wichita Police said she was released "pending the results of toxicology testing and a mechanical examination of the vehicle." Police said in a statement Tuesday that they have interviewed nearly 50 witnesses, with more interviews ongoing. "Investigators are also inspecting the truck, analyzing available vehicle data and continuing investigative work at Stryker Sports Complex," police said. "They are working closely with the Regional Forensic Science Center and awaiting official, peer-reviewed toxicology results." The driver remained at the scene and has been cooperative, they said. "Based on the information available Sunday morning, and after consultation with the Sedgwick County District Attorney’s Office, investigators did not have probable cause to arrest the driver. She was released, and the investigation remains ongoing. Her release does not represent a final determination about whether criminal charges are appropriate." LISTEN: KANSAS SOCCER FIELD DISPATCH CALL CAPTURES MASS-CASUALTY RESPONSE AFTER DRIVER KILLS BOY, MAN "We know that this case has captured the attention of people all over the country, and many of those people have strong opinions about the incident even though they do not have direct knowledge of what occurred," Chief Joe Sullivan said. "We recognize that the decision the law and constitution required us to make on Sunday morning may not be popular. We swear an oath to support the laws of the State of Kansas and the Constitution of the United States and no one in the Wichita Police Department takes that oath for granted." The driver had a valid driver’s license and no outstanding arrest warrants, police said. They dispelled rumors circulating online, noting that the driver is not in the country illegally, has no documented criminal history, and no association with the Wichita Police Department, the Sedgwick County Sheriff’s Office or any other law enforcement agency. Andrew Ford, a spokesperson for the Wichita Police Department, told TMZ that the driver was interviewed for several hours after the crash. He said she answered questions about what happened, according to the outlet. Ford told TMZ that police are investigating all possibilities about why this happened, including whether speeding, mechanical failure, or drugs or alcohol played a factor. Wichita police could not immediately be reached for comment. Did the driver suffer a medical emergency? No information on the driver's medical condition at the time of the crash has been released. Copenhaver said it may be necessary for law enforcement to release information on the woman's physical health condition at the time of the incident to "prevent conspiracy theories." "People need to know a little bit more transparency as to why this may have occurred," he said. Did her vehicle malfunction? Police said that the black pickup truck involved in the incident was going to undergo mechanical testing. Copenhaver said the black box will be able to give a better idea of whether something went mechanically wrong before the deadly crash. He said the data will reveal possible "contributing factors" like speed, whether she hit the brakes, timing of the braking and how far the vehicle may have skidded. ACCUSED TEEN KILLER'S OWN DASHCAM COULD PROVE MURDER OF TWO GIRLS MOWED DOWN, LAWYER SAYS: 'NOT AN ACCIDENT' "It doesn't take that long, in my opinion, to download that data, have one of their experts go over it," he said. Copenhaver went on to say, "If there's an issue with that truck, that computer is going to alert the examiner or the expert that's looking at this data." 📩 Send me a story idea: kelsie.cairns@fox.com 📸 Instagram: kelsiecairns_tv 🎥 Facebook: Kelsie Cairns TEXAS WOMAN SENTENCED TO 7 YEARS IN PRISON, ANNUAL JAIL TIME DURING PROBATION FOR DEADLY DUI CRASH Why is the toxicology taking so long? Copenhaver said in his experience results from alcohol-related DUI testing usually comes back within a day. FLORIDA WOMAN ACCUSED OF DUI CRASHES SUV INTO PARKED CAR, THEN MAKES BIZARRE PLEA TO POLICE CAUGHT ON CAMERA "If it's alcohol-related, they're going to know instantaneously," he said. He added, "Once that blood draw is taken, once it's ran through the machines [investigators] will be able to tell you if an individual is under the influence of alcohol." He said testing for other substances like hard drugs or medications can take significantly longer. Those require "specialty testing," he said. There is also a possibility that the woman may have been taking prescription medication, which could have impacted her driving, he said. Testing for that is "longer than that normal blood draw," he said. GOT A TIP? SEND US A TIP In a statement sent to Fox News Digital, the Wichita Police Department shot down questions circulating on social media about whether there was a law enforcement connection. "The Wichita Police Department is aware of false information circulating on social media regarding this investigation, including a rumor alleging that a Sedgwick County Sheriff's Office deputy was involved," the department said in part. "The Sheriff's Office has publicly addressed that allegation and identified it as false." GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL The department went on to say, "We ask everyone to be responsible with what they share, consider the harm misinformation can cause and allow investigators to do their work based on facts and evidence, not speculation." articles.title: In rare disclosure, China reveals advanced nuclear subs in Pacific test; a look inside its submarine fleet
articles.summary: China has revealed that its most advanced nuclear-powered submarines were used to test-fire a strategic missile in the Pacific earlier this year, offering
articles.body: China has revealed that its most advanced nuclear-powered submarines were used to test-fire a strategic missile in the Pacific earlier this year, offering a rare glimpse into Beijing’s expanding undersea nuclear capabilities as it seeks to strengthen its military reach and strategic deterrence in the Indo-Pacific.According to a Bloomberg report, China’s state-run Xinhua News Agency said that the third generation of its Changzheng-series nuclear submarines had successfully conducted a test launch of a submarine-launched strategic missile.The announcement, accompanied by an image of the July test, marks the first public confirmation that Beijing deployed its latest-generation submarines for the launch.The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) did not disclose the type of submarine or missile used in the test, leaving key details of the launch unclear. Analysts had earlier speculated that the missile was fired from a Type 094 Jin-class ballistic missile submarine, but Beijing’s latest statement points to the possible involvement of a more advanced generation of nuclear submarines.The July launch demonstrated the sea-based component of China’s nuclear triad, which also includes land-based missiles and nuclear-capable aircraft.Submarine-launched ballistic missiles are a crucial part of a country’s nuclear deterrent because they can be fired from vessels operating underwater, making them harder for adversaries to detect and potentially improving the ability to retaliate following a nuclear attack.China had conducted only two publicly known intercontinental ballistic missile tests in the Pacific before the July launch, both involving land-based systems.The latest disclosure highlights the growing role of its submarine fleet in strategic weapons testing, although Beijing has not confirmed whether the missile used in July was nuclear-armed or disclosed its range and technical specifications.Inside China’s growing nuclear submarine fleetChina is rapidly expanding its nuclear-powered submarine fleet, combining new vessel construction with longer-range submarine-launched missiles to strengthen its ability to project military power across the Indo-Pacific.An assessment published by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) in February 2026 said China launched more nuclear-powered submarines, in both number and combined tonnage, than the United States during 2021–25, although qualitative differences between their fleets remain.The expansion spans two distinct capabilities: ballistic missile submarines, which underpin China’s sea-based nuclear deterrent, and attack submarines designed to target enemy vessels and extend naval operations beyond China’s coastal waters.China’s current ballistic missile submarine force is centred on the Type 094 Jin-class, which carries up to 12 submarine-launched ballistic missiles.The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, in its Chinese Nuclear Weapons, 2026 assessment published on July 8, estimated that China operated six Type 094 submarines, while noting the development of the next-generation Type 096.The IISS, using commercial satellite imagery and other open-source evidence, assessed in February that China had likely launched seventh and eighth Type 094 boats in 2024 and 2025, respectively.A key part of the programme is the development of longer-range submarine-launched ballistic missiles. China has been replacing the JL-2, assessed to have a range of around 7,200 kilometres, with the JL-3, which is designed to extend the reach of its sea-based nuclear force.Beyond its ballistic missile submarines, China is expanding its nuclear-powered attack submarine force. The Type 093B Shang III class is assessed to carry vertical-launch cells for guided missiles, expanding the Chinese navy’s options for attacking surface ships and potentially striking targets at longer ranges.The next-generation Type 095 is associated with the development of more capable nuclear-powered attack submarines, while the Type 096 is expected to succeed the Type 094 as a ballistic missile platform.The expansion is also changing how US naval intelligence assesses the long-term challenge posed by China.Rear Admiral Michael Brookes, commander of the US Office of Naval Intelligence, told the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission in March 2026 that “By 2040, the PLA Navy’s undersea forces may credibly challenge US regional maritime dominance, complicating crisis response, power projection and allied defense.”USNI News reported that Brookes projected that up to half of China’s anticipated 80-boat attack submarine fleet could be nuclear-powered by 2035.

articles.title: Army's top brass meets in Delhi to review modernisation, security and readiness
articles.summary: The Army Commanders' Conference, the apex biannual forum of the army, began in New Delhi on October 21 and runs until October 23.
articles.body: The Army Commanders' Conference, the apex biannual forum of the army, began in New Delhi on October 21 and runs until October 23. It brings together the army's senior leadership to discuss the evolving security environment, operational preparedness, capability development and transformation initiatives. This is the first such conference chaired by General Dhiraj Seth, who took over as the 31st Chief of the Army Staff on June 30, 2026, succeeding General Upendra Dwivedi.Defence minister Rajnath Singh will address the conference on the final day. The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Raja Subramani, Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and the secretary of the ministry of electronics and information Technology will also speak on contemporary security issues. The army's land warfare doctrine will be released by the defence minister, which is meant to give the force an overarching framework for the changing character of warfare and future conflicts. The defence minister will also unveil the annual United Nations Journal and felicitate Army personnel who have made notable contributions as UN peacekeepers.The agenda follows the usual pattern for these meetings, the army's leadership will review the security situation along the country's borders, the regional and global environment, terrorism as well as other emerging challenges. They look at operational readiness, including deployment, logistics, infrastructure and the ability to respond to different conflict scenarios. Modernisation and weapons are discussed, covering new equipment, procurement, technology, surveillance, drones, counter-drone systems and capability gaps, along with lessons from ongoing international conflicts and recent operations. Defence indigenisation, personnel policy, training, welfare, financial management and organisational reforms are also on the table, as are proposed changes to doctrine, force structure and modernisation plans.The previous conference was held in New Delhi from April 13 to 16, 2026, under the previous army chief General Upendra Dwivedi, who has since retired. Discussions in that meet had focused on modernisation, technology in combat operations, training and doctrine, and operational lessons from Operation Sindoor, with unmanned aerial systems and counter-unmanned aerial systems among the capability areas examined. The Army has designated 2026 as the year of Networking and Data Centricity, under its broader goal of becoming a future-ready force, and the April meeting also stressed the need to speed up indigenous defence production and strengthen coordination between military and civilian institutions.General Seth will also confer awards for green military stations and aviation flight safety, recognising environmental sustainability, resource management and a strong aviation safety culture. The conference is meant to let the Army's senior leadership review ongoing initiatives, identify future thrust areas and set policy directions for a technologically enabled, adaptive and future-ready force.

articles.title: Woman told Russell Brand he 'treated her like an animal', court hears
articles.summary: The comedian and actor is on trial for charges including rape and sexual assault, which he denies.
articles.body:
Warning - this report contains graphic content

One of the women who claims Russell Brand raped her later told him he had "treated her like an animal", a court has heard.

The comedian's trial at Southwark Crown Court in London has been hearing recorded police interviews with a female complainant, who claims she did not consent to anal sex with him at his house in 2009.

Brand, 51, denies three charges of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one charge of indecent assault. He has said he has never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity.

The allegations span a 10-year period from 1999 to 2009 and involve six female complainants.

On Wednesday, the jury heard an interview with a woman who says she first met Brand at one of his comedy shows at Hammersmith Apollo in 2009.

She said she had a boyfriend at the time but went to his dressing room, where she performed a sex act on him.

The woman said it was during their next meeting at his house when the sex was not consensual and she had only agreed to vaginal sex.

Asked by the detective in the interview whether there was ever a conversation about anal sex, she replied: "No."

She said she was surprised to receive a "random" text message from Brand six months later, saying he wanted to "push her further".

She said she replied asking: "Why are you even messaging me?"

"I remember his response, saying, 'Because you're dirty and I want to push you further'."

The jury heard that the woman did not respond straight away because she was upset, but then replied saying: "I think you've pushed me far enough, you treated me like an animal."

The woman added: "I do remember his response was immediate. He said, 'I'm sorry'."

During cross-examination, the woman was asked by defence barrister Ian Winter KC about her decision to meet Brand.

"You made it clear that you went to his house to have sex with him, knowing his reputation," he said.

She said that was "correct", adding: "I want to flag that I wanted to go there, I take ownership."

The woman said she had a couple of glasses of alcohol while getting ready at home and another glass while waiting in a restaurant for Brand's driver to pick her up on the day of the alleged rape.

The court heard he made her shower and brush her teeth before they had sex.

Winter suggested that Brand asked her to do so because he did not like the smell of alcohol "because of his soberism", but the woman said it was because "he didn't like the smell of my hair".

When questioning her about the alleged rape, Winter put to the female complainant: "You had vaginal sex with a condom on and then it finished with you agreeing to anal sex."

The woman replied: "I did not consent to that at that time.

"We're not here to discuss my morality. We're here to discuss criminality. I thought I was going to have penetrative vaginal sex.

She broke down in tears at the end of giving her evidence.

articles.title: La Hexagon World Series y sus cambios para 2027: tres sedes más, nuevo formato y la entrada de Emiratos Árabes
articles.standfirst: El circuito de pádel por equipos sigue innovando y creciendo alrededor del mundo
articles.summary: El circuito de pádel por equipos sigue innovando y creciendo alrededor del mundo
articles.body: La nueva Hexagon World Series ha presentado este miércoles en el hotel Emirates Palaces Mandarin Oriental de Abu Dhabi (Emiratos Árabes Unidos) sus grandes novedades para el calendario de 2027, donde refuerza su apuesta por el formato de pádel por equipos y con las que se consolida como 'plato fuerte' dentro del calendario FIP y de Premier Padel. Tras tres ediciones de Hexagon Cup celebradas en Madrid, ahora se volverá a arrancar con la prueba en la capital de España, donde se disputará del 21 al 24 de enero de 2027 en la Caja Mágica. La capital española será así el punto de partida de un nuevo circuito internacional que aspira a llevar el formato por equipos a una nueva dimensión. Pero para el próximo año las novedades son tres. Una de ellas, la más importante: nuevas sedes. Hexagon viajará hacia Norte América con otra prueba en el mes de marzo. Luego, en el mes de junio, llegarán a Escandinavia, y después, en octubre, cerrará la temporada en Emiratos Árabes Unidos. Tres nuevas plazas -de las que se conocerá el país concreto en las próximas semanas- en las que los mejores jugadores y jugadoras del planeta se darán cita. Y lo harán, eso sí, con un nuevo formato en los partidos. Se dejará a un lado el método de puntuación tradicional, que en la Hexagon incluía la particularidad de decidir los partidos que fuesen a un tercer set con un súper tiebreak. Ahora, en 2027, los partidos se jugarán al mejor de cinco súper tiebreaks. Es decir, que cada set concluirá cuando una de las parejas llegue a 10 puntos, con el objetivo de dinamizar aún más los enfrentamientos y la competición en sí. Como última novedad está la entrada de un nuevo equipo, esta vez con sello de Emiratos Árabes, que se unirá a varios de los clásicos que han participado en las ediciones pasadas. Seguirán AD/vantage Team, Bella Puerto Rico, Eleven Eleven, KRU Padel, Rafa Nadal Academy Team, 10 Padel y Hexagon Team. Durante la presentación, Enrique Buenaventura, cofundador de Hexagon, se mostró ilusionado con esta nueva etapa. "Estamos deseando empezar. Ya se ha visto estos años en Madrid que es algo diferente, divertido y entretenido. Hemos trabajado bajo el paraguas de Premier Padel y FIP para encajar estas pruebas en el calendario", afirmó. Sergio Lewin, cofundador y Managing Director en Hexagon World Series, incidió en el cambio de formato, con sello propio y con el objetivo de consolidar la competición con una identidad reconocible. "Queremos innovar, y el nuevo formato viene por ahí. Buscamos partidos de más intensidad, hemos hablado con los jugadores y están encantados. Será divertido", explicó.

articles.title: Cumbria zoo welcomes 'troublesome' trio of rare baby fossas
articles.summary: Lakeland Wildlife Oasis says the triplets' arrival is a "very big step towards fossa conservation".
articles.body:
Zoo staff have been left "over the moon" after welcoming a trio of rare baby fossas.

The triplets were born at Lakeland Wildlife Oasis in Milnthorpe, Cumbria, about three months ago and can now be seen by visitors.

Animal manager Dan Eccles said they were the only ones born in the UK this year and only one other zoo in Europe had bred them so far in 2026.

"I honestly think I could sit and watch them for hours," he said. "They are brilliant, brilliant little things."

Fossas are native to Madagascar and are currently listed as vulnerable to extinction by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).

Despite looking like cats, they are more related to mongooses.

The species is also rare in captivity and there are only about 15 in UK zoos, Eccles said.

Lakeland Wildlife Oasis staff had a tight window of only a few days during breeding season when future parents Mango and Makira would tolerate each other.

"You don't just put them together and be done with it," Eccles said.

"They are quite aggressive with each other as well, the male and the female don't typically live together, we have to mix them very carefully at a very precise time of year to make sure that they're actually receptive to each other."

He said staff were "over the moon" when the triplets were born, adding it was a "very big step towards fossa conservation".

An announcement from the zoo described the playful trio as "troublesome".

Eccles said they were "constantly" wrestling and climbing, putting their mum's patience to the test.

"I really don't understand how Makira, the female, puts up with them sometimes because they just never stop," he said.

"The only time they stop is when they are asleep.

"Thankfully they do sleep for part of the day, because I don't think Makira would manage otherwise."

The pups are born blind and toothless and reach maturity after two to four years.

They typically live between 15 and 20 years.

It is estimated that as few as 2,500 fossas remain in the wild.

articles.title: Extension plans put forward for historic Jersey War Tunnels
articles.summary: The plans include an extension to the visitor centre and the demolition of a single-storey building.
articles.body:
An historic World War Two tunnel attraction has put forward extension plans for its museum and site.

Jersey War Tunnels hopes to extend the museum into the existing car park and change the parking arrangements. It follows a consultation process that asked people about improvements they would like to see at the site.

The hillside tunnels were constructed during World War Two by enslaved workers from across Europe during the Occupation of the Channel Islands.

The plans said the extension of the site aimed to provide extra exhibit and museum space for important historical items which could not be housed in the "unsuitable tunnel environment". The proposals will be discussed at a later date.

The plans include an extension to the visitor centre building and the demolition of a single-storey office building.

TSA, which has been appointed to develop the plans, said the scheme did not propose to make any alterations within the historically listed underground tunnel complex.

The proposals included road safety changes, with designated pedestrian routes and crossings.

articles.title: Belfast comedian Vittorio Angelone criticised for rape "joke"
articles.summary: Vittorio Angelone referred to content creator Rebecca Goodwin in a remark about rape.
articles.body:
A Belfast comedian has been criticised for making a rape "joke" about a woman who had recently spoken publicly about being the victim of a sexual assault.

Vittorio Angelone, who has since apologised on social media, referred to content creator Rebecca Goodwin in a remark about rape which he made in a podcast episode in 2025.

Goodwin, who had previously reported a rape to police, said it will "forever live with me that it was allowed for my name to be used as the punchline of a malicious "joke" about such a serious issue".

Angelone said he has reached out to Goodwin and apologised directly.

Goodwin had claimed that Angelone posted videos of the "joke" on his social media accounts in recent days.

Rape Crisis Northern Ireland and Dublin Rape Crisis Centre have both criticised the remarks.

The makers of the podcast have been contacted for comment.

During a 2025 episode of the 'Have a Word' podcast, Angelone asked of fellow comedian Freddy Quinne "if you're here, who's raping Rebecca Goodwin?".

British OnlyFans creator Rebecca Goodwin had previously spoken publicly about being the victim of sexual assault.

The comments were made during a "roast" episode of the podcast posted in December 2025.

The episode, which Goodwin was not involved in, contained comedians taking turns insulting each other in front of an audience.

In a post on Facebook, Goodwin said the episode was recorded "in September/October of 2025 and has been behind a paywall for a year before being published to social media".

She reported a rape to police in July 2025 and had spoken publicly about her experience.

Goodwin said she only became aware of the comments when clips were posted to social media in recent days.

"I am grateful I never saw it sooner because it would've been just weeks after [the assault] happened and I was in a different mental state to what I am now," she said.

At that time, Goodwin said that "no contact or apology has been attempted" by Angelone, but that he had "removed the joke from his own social media, again, over a year after it was made, edited, clipped, captioned and posted with my full name included".

The comments have not been edited out of the paywalled episode of the podcast.

Goodwin said: "We are facing a global crisis of violence against women and girls, and we are begging for our safety and experiences to be taken seriously."

She added that Freddy Quinne, as well as a number of other comedians who were part of the podcast episode, had since apologised to her.

However, Goodwin said that she did not accept the apologies as they "only came a year after the joke was made and nobody had my back in that room at the time, up until I made a social media post about it".

In a statement on Instagram, Angelone said he let his "need for validation supersede my own standards and morals".

"It's completely pathetic and I'm ashamed to realise that about myself," he said.

Angelone will feature in his first major acting role in upcoming BBC sitcom Rewarding, which is set to air this autumn.

BBC Northern Ireland have been approached for comment.

'When rape becomes a punchline, it's harder for survivors to speak out'

Rape Crisis Northern Ireland said they were "very disappointed to hear of the comments made by Vittorio Angelone which contribute to a culture in which rape and sexual violence can be trivialised".

"When rape becomes a punchline and sexual violence is treated as entertainment, it becomes easier to dismiss its impact and harder for survivors to speak out."

It continued: "Those with a public platform and an audience have a responsibility to consider the impact of the language they use and the attitudes they help to normalise.

"Rape jokes might seem far removed from an act of sexual violence, but they sit within that same culture of minimising and trivialising it."

They added "survivors should never be left feeling that what happened to them is something that could be laughed at, minimised or dismissed".

Chief Executive of Dublin Rape Crisis Centre, Rachel Morrogh, said: "For survivors, hearing rape treated as a punchline can be deeply hurtful, and it reinforces the attitudes that discourage people from coming forward.

"Anyone with a public platform, including performers, promoters and venues, has a responsibility to consider who is listening and the harm this kind of material can do. To treat sexual violence as a joke betrays a deep lack of understanding of what survivors have lived through."

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line .

articles.title: Pakistani authorities arrest man accused in $126m US postage fraud
articles.summary: Faheem Akram has been charged with several offences including conspiracy to defraud the United States.
articles.body:
Pakistani authorities have arrested a man accused of masterminding an online counterfeit operation that United States prosecutors say resulted in more than $125m of losses to the US Postal Service.

Faheem Akram, 33, was arrested on Tuesday after an expansive search operation and raids across Pakistan, a senior official at the Pakistani National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency told reporters.

Akram was indicted last month by a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida, and is accused of operating a fraudulent website where he sold more than 5.1 million counterfeit stamps in the US.

The stamps, which cost about $2 each, allowed customers to ship their packages at a lower price than official postal rates, causing significant losses to the Postal Service, according to the US Attorney’s office.

The estimate of more than $124m however, represents the losses to the Postal Service and not the proceeds from the website, officials said.

Pakistani investigators discovered that Akram has been operating the website since August 2023 and used 16 bank accounts, including his own and several family members’, for the operation.

Akram has been charged with several offences, including conspiracy to defraud the US and the making and selling of fake postage stamps, as well as four counts of wire fraud, according to the US Postal Service.

He could face 20 years in prison on each count of wire fraud, as well as five years in prison for conspiracy.

Akram is currently in custody in Pakistan, but it is unclear whether he will face trial in the country or be extradited to the US.

articles.title: After 12 years of demolition threats, residents of two 1960s London housing estates may finally keep their homes; Lambeth Council has proposed abandoning the rebuild plans, with a cabinet decision due October 21
articles.summary: Residents of two landmark 1960s housing estates in south London may finally be able to remain in their homes after more than 12 years of uncertainty.
articles.body: Residents of two landmark 1960s housing estates in south London may finally be able to remain in their homes after more than 12 years of uncertainty. Lambeth Council has proposed removing Central Hill in Crystal Palace and Cressingham Gardens beside Brockwell Park from its demolition and redevelopment programme, choosing instead to retain, repair and improve the existing homes. The proposal will be considered by the council’s Cabinet on October 21, according to Lambeth Council and The Guardian.A major shift in policyThe new plans would end the long-running threat of demolition for Central Hill and Cressingham Gardens, both of which are known for their distinctive postwar design, green spaces and established communities. Instead of rebuilding the estates from scratch, Lambeth wants to invest in existing homes, bring empty properties back into use and protect the neighbourhoods that residents have created over decades.Council officers found that comprehensive redevelopment of both estates was financially unviable. That conclusion has led the council to recommend a different approach, one that keeps the existing homes in place while still seeking ways to increase the supply of genuinely affordable council and social housing.The proposals would also remove Knights Walk and Trinity Rise from the New Homes Hexagon Portfolio. At Knights Walk, the completed first phase has left the proposed second-phase site inaccessible, making the remaining scheme unviable, as per the reports.Relief after years of uncertaintyFor residents, the announcement represents the possibility of stability after years of living under the threat of losing their homes. Many have campaigned against demolition, arguing that the estates are not merely collections of buildings but communities with long-standing social ties, shared histories and a strong sense of place.Councillor Pete Elliott, Lambeth’s Cabinet Member for Housing, said, according to the reports, that the proposals would end years of uncertainty and put the focus on repairing homes, supporting communities and filling empty properties. He said the council had fought for a better future for Central Hill and Cressingham Gardens for more than 12 years.Councillor Scott Ainslie, Cabinet Member for Property, Planning and Development, Built Environment and Public Realm, said the estates are valued places with strong communities and distinctive architecture. He added that the council had stood with residents in arguing that their future should not depend on demolition, reported Lambeth Council.Protecting architectural heritageCentral Hill and Cressingham Gardens are important examples of 1960s social housing design. Their retention would preserve not only homes but also an architectural legacy created by an earlier generation of planners and designers.Lambeth Council leader Councillor Martin Abrams described the proposal as a decisive moment for the two estates. He said it recognised the work involved in securing their future without demolition, while allowing investment to focus on residents’ homes and the reuse of empty properties.The council says it can build the homes Lambeth needs without erasing the best of what earlier generations created. Its new programme will pursue high-quality and sustainable council and social housing on suitable sites, using every viable delivery model.Building homes another wayAlthough the council is stepping back from wholesale demolition, it says the need for more affordable homes remains urgent. Lambeth plans to use a broader range of delivery routes, including buying homes and delivering new council housing directly.The council will also identify suitable small sites and infill opportunities across the borough. These smaller developments could add homes without requiring the clearance of large existing estates, offering a more targeted way to expand housing supply.Residents will also be involved in future plans for other estates. Lambeth will work with the community on proposals for the Westbury estate in Clapham Town, which could deliver hundreds of new homes, including more genuinely affordable homes. It will also review options for the Fenwick Estate in Clapham North and develop options for the South Lambeth estate with residents.What happens nextThe Cabinet will consider the proposals on October 21. Residents are due to receive a letter, and updates will be published on each estate’s website before the meeting.If approved, the decision would be a significant victory for campaigners who have spent years opposing demolition. It would also signal a wider shift in how some London boroughs approach estate renewal, placing repair, community retention and architectural preservation alongside the need to build new homes.More detail on Lambeth’s New Homes Programme, including reviews of the remaining sites and plans for new council and social housing, is expected later this year. articles.title: South Korean officials free a shark trapped for a month in Busan canal
articles.summary: After failed attempts in recent weeks, South Korean officials on Wednesday finally freed a large gray shark that had been trapped for more than a month in a canal in the port city of Busan.
articles.body: SEOUL, South Korea — After failed attempts in recent weeks, South Korean officials on Wednesday finally freed a large gray shark that had been trapped for more than a month in a canal in the port city of Busan. Officials used a floating platform to herd the nearly 10-foot female dusky shark, nicknamed Bukangi after the Korean name for Busan’s North Port, along the narrow canal for hours. The shark lingered at the canal’s mouth but eventually swam to sea, Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo said. The shark was first spotted in mid-September and became a major tourist attraction as it slowly circled the canal, its fins slicing through the water’s surface. Busan officials, who made Bukangi a city mascot, said the shark attracted more than 1.7 million visitors to the canal. But they struggled for weeks to find a way to guide it back to the open sea. Wednesday’s operation was the third attempt to free Bukangi, following failed efforts on Sept. 29 and Oct. 2 that involved boats spraying streams of water and nets placed across the narrow waterway. The shark avoided the boats and swam over the nets. Experts have raised concerns about the shark’s condition, saying it had shown no signs of feeding during its monthlong stay in the canal and that falling water temperatures posed additional health risks. Wednesday’s operation involved painstakingly maneuvering a large floating platform through the canal to drive the shark out. Workers stood on the platform and used oars to push Bukangi back whenever it approached. Dozens of other workers on both banks pulled ropes to drag the structure forward, as hundreds of onlookers lined the canal to watch the highly unusual rescue effort. Workers managed to push the platform about a kilometer (0.6 miles) toward the mouth of the canal and placed additional netting in front of the structure to prevent the shark from swimming back in. It wasn’t immediately clear how far the shark swam out and South Korea’s Yonhap news agency reported that it was seen at a nearby pier. “We will never forget the great interest people have shown for Bukangi and Busan’s waters,” Chun wrote on Facebook. “We hope Bukangi can live a healthy life in the blue sea.”
